body:
@yyx990803 Is that problem reproducible without a side-effect in the computed (or in render)? I can't find a way, at least.

If it's not, then as a theoretical question: Should we really support that? Or is it that we don't want to but need to support it to keep backwards compat for something that worked even though [it has always been a discouraged practice](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/computed.html#getters-should-be-side-effect-free)?
This is indeed discouraged usage, but this is a regression nonetheless and should ideally be fixed.

> Simplified reproduction:
> 
> https://play.vuejs.org/#

@yyx990803 I think this reproduction appears to have the correct output (computed didn't calculate until the render function, and `state.a` was changed to 1 before it was tracked)
@Doctor-wu `state.a` should be tracked regardless, and `state.a = 2` should trigger component re-render.

> @Doctor-wu `state.a` should be tracked regardless, and `state.a = 2` should trigger component re-render.

@yyx990803 `state.a` was indeed tracked, but timing is key. Computes are lazily calculated. When `c.value` was accessed, the process had already arrived at the `render` function, which is after the `setup` function that executes `state.a = 2`. In other words, when `state.a = 2` is executed, there is no effect tracked by `state.a`.
You are looking at an outdated repro, there is a `setTimeout` (I edited the link a few times)

> You are looking at an outdated repro, there is a `setTimeout` (I edited the link a few times)

That's true😂, I'll check the new one.

I think the key to this problem is the `computed` was mutated in render lead the `computed` was marked to `Dirty` after the invocation of the `render` function. And I think that is a dangerous state of `computed` (marked as dirty, which means it won't be reactive anymore)
